content.text:
Here are **notable art collaborations from 2023**, especially where visual art crossed into fashion, museums, public art, and design:

| Collaboration | What it was |
|---|---|
| **Louis Vuitton × Yayoi Kusama** | One of 2023’s biggest art-fashion collaborations, with Kusama’s signature polka dots applied to Louis Vuitton bags, shoes, apparel, fragrances, and global store installations. ([usaartnews.com](https://usaartnews.com/news/artistic-collaborations-2023?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Dior × Mickalene Thomas** | For Dior’s Spring 2023 couture presentation, artist Mickalene Thomas created collage-based works celebrating Black women, tied to a Josephine Baker–inspired show. ([harpersbazaar.com](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/fashion/fashion-week/a42634749/mickalene-thomas-dior-couture-spring-2023/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Loewe × Studio Ghibli / Howl’s Moving Castle** | Loewe continued its art-and-animation partnership with Studio Ghibli in 2023 through a collection based on *Howl’s Moving Castle*. ([marieclaire.co.uk](https://www.marieclaire.co.uk/fashion/7-iconic-fashion-art-hype-collaborations?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Louis Vuitton Men’s Fall 2023 creative collective** | The show involved a group of creatives, including designer **Colm “KidSuper” Dillane** and filmmakers **Michel and Olivier Gondry**, blending fashion, film, performance, and visual storytelling. ([goat.com](https://www.goat.com/editorial/2023-the-year-in-collaborations?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Guggenheim Museum × Converse** | Announced in 2023 as a global partnership connecting contemporary art, youth culture, education, and artist-led programming. ([guggenheim.org](https://www.guggenheim.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/press-release-converse-guggenheim-global-partnership-announcement-20231109.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MoMA digital art collaborations** | MoMA announced a slate of digital-art acquisitions, exhibitions, and artist collaborations in fall 2023–winter 2024, including work connected to generative and digital art. ([press.moma.org](https://press.moma.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/MoMADigitalArtAnnouncements_FINAL-2.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Beyond Granite: Pulling Together** | A major collaborative public-art initiative on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., curated by Monument Lab and organized with the Trust for the National Mall, the National Capital Planning Commission, and the National Park Service. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_Granite%3A_Pulling_Together?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Met Museum × beauty/design brands** | The Met continued licensing collaborations with beauty, fragrance, and design brands, using artworks from its collection to create consumer products tied back to museum history. ([harpersbazaar.com](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/beauty/makeup/a41780213/art-museums-beauty-collaborations/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Art Basel Miami 2023 fashion collaborations** | Miami Art Week saw multiple fashion-art activations and collaborations, with luxury brands using Art Basel as a platform for installations, events, and limited-edition projects. ([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/cassellferere/2023/12/07/heres-how-fashion-is-showing-up-at-art-basel-miami-2023/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Lanvin Lab × Future** | A 2023 fashion-music-art collaboration in which Lanvin invited rapper Future to create an exclusive collection under its Lanvin Lab concept. ([fashionunited.com](https://fashionunited.com/news/fashion/best-of-2023-collaborations-of-the-year/2023122957595?utm_source=openai)) |

If you mean **“art collaborations” in music**—like songs by artists featuring other artists from 2023—I can make a separate list of the biggest 2023 music collaborations.
